extracted.intended_audience: Researchers and investigators preparing or managing NIH grant applications (R01, R21, K awards, R56, R35, K99, etc.) seeking practical funding-process guidance
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, experience-based guidance for applying to and managing NIH grants (timing, paylines, JIT, resubmissions, R56 mechanics, interactions with Program Officers and Grants Management). Includes timelines and rules for common mechanisms (R01, R21, K, R56, R35, K99).

rubrics_metrics.name: R56 and R01 A1 funding interplay
rubrics_metrics.description: If an R56 is awarded and an A1 is later awarded, remaining R56 funds are applied to the R01 A1 period rather than added on top of the A1 award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from the page: "if you ask for $300K in Year 1 of the R01 A1, and there is $150K left on the R56, you would get a total of $300K for the April 2022 through March 2023 R01 A1 period, with $150K coming from the R56 and $150K coming from the R01 A1 (you would not get $450K … $300K A1 + $150K R56). If the A1 is not awarded, the R56 would continue through August-September 2022." Use this when budgeting and planning how R56 bridge funding will affect subsequent R01 budgets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic considerations beyond score
rubrics_metrics.description: Institutes may consider programmatic balance and other priorities (not strictly score order) when making awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: "NHLBI makes 4-7 awards per year, so the key is whether they go strictly by score or also consider programmatic interest (to avoid funding 4 awards in the same general research area...)." Expect small-program ICs to use programmatic judgment in addition to score percentiles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact your Program Officer (PO) for institute-specific intel
rubrics_metrics.description: The PO is the best source for up-to-date, institute-specific information on paylines, funding likelihood, and next steps after summary statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice repeated throughout: ask your PO about payline expectations, FOA Notices, whether to resubmit, and JIT or award timing. Also check archived pages and IC-specific documentation, but treat the PO as the primary contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rebuttal letters are optional and not uniformly used
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for a rebuttal (1–2 page PI response) are not required across NIH and their presence/absence is not a reliable signal of funding likelihood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote: "No, requesting a rebuttal is not a requirement and is not uniformly used." Historically became more common recently (e.g., at NCI). Do not assume that being asked for a rebuttal guarantees funding, nor that not being asked means you will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of success rates vs percentiles
rubrics_metrics.description: Success rate is calculated differently from percentile-based paylines and is not directly equivalent to percentile score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted definition: "A success rate is roughly the number of applications funded by an institute divided by the number of peer reviewed applications referred to it (excluding resubmissions that occur in the same fiscal year—each application is counted only once)." Note that success rate (SR) is usually higher than percentile; use institute-specific stats to interpret your chance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council approves but IC Director makes final funding decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Council votes to approve applications to be considered for funding; the IC Director has the final authority to award and signs NOAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote guidance: "Advisory Council approves applications to be considered for funding, but the IC Director makes all final funding decisions." POs may advocate for borderline applications, but final decisions reflect IC priorities and available appropriation.

rubrics_metrics.name: JIT requests and their meaning (automated vs personal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Just-in-Time (JIT) requests are frequently issued for many applications; an automated JIT does not guarantee funding, while a targeted/personal JIT is a stronger signal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: "ICs request JIT for more applications than they can fund just to be sure they have enough award-ready ones." Receipt of JIT (especially a personal JIT) signals interest but not finality. Complete JIT materials promptly when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Commons status interpretation (Council review completed → pending)
rubrics_metrics.description: The status 'Council review completed' (often shown in grey) typically precedes a change to 'pending administrative review' and is not necessarily cause for concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote: "The status will almost always change to the grey 'council review completed' before changing to 'pending'. It could stay that way for several weeks and is nothing to worry about." Do not panic at a greyed Council status; monitor and, if needed, contact PO after reasonable waiting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and NOA timing relative to fiscal year end
rubrics_metrics.description: NOAs can be issued up to Sept 30 (end of the federal fiscal year); many awards are processed throughout September but often wrap up ~10 days prior to year-end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes: "They can issue NoAs all the way until Sept 30, but most are wrapped up about 10 days prior to that." If expecting an award near FY-end, keep PO/GMS informed but avoid excessive interruptions during the busy month.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check FOA Application Types and associated Notices
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) does not list 'Resubmission' as an allowed application type, A1s are not allowed — but Notices associated with the FOA can modify allowed types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice: "You should always look at all the Notices associated with any FOA." If there's confusion, contact your PO before preparing an A1. Do not assume a FOA's Section II is immutable without checking Notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission strategy: resubmit if in doubt
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is any doubt about whether an A0 will be funded, resubmitting (A1) is generally recommended because the time lost by waiting may be costly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted advisory: "Even then, I usually recommend resubmitting if there is any doubt about the A0 being funded. The time lost is too valuable..." Use resubmission to address reviewer concerns and strengthen the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing Revision (competitive supplement) rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Competing revisions can only be submitted if the FOA that funded the original R01 accepts revision applications; many revision awards are for 1 year but confirm with PO and FOA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance: "Check Section II. Award Information for the FOA through which your R01 was funded. If the FOA accepts revision applications, then you apply through the same FOA; if not, you cannot submit a revision application... I believe most revision awards are for 1 year, though you can talk with your PO about this as well."

rubrics_metrics.name: R56 mechanics and implications for future R01 submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: An R56 bridge award can be issued in lieu of funding an R01 A0/A1 and has specific implications for subsequent submissions (A1 may be withdrawn; you may submit a new A0 later).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points pulled from the page and IC SOPs: "The ultimate goal of the award is to provide interim, one-year support for investigators to collect preliminary data in support of a resubmission or newly competing NIH R01 application." Also: when an A0 is converted to an R56 the A1 may be withdrawn ("Withdrawn by IC – Other Version Encumbered"). You can later submit a new A0 (not an A1) and the R56 counts as other support; you may carry over R56 funds to an R01 if awarded as a resubmission. Clarify allowable overlap with PO before submitting the next R01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication etiquette with PO and Grants Management (GMS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be judicious in contacting PO/GMS during busy periods; POs can't handle grants management tasks and frequent interruptions can slow processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advice from page: "There is no benefit in trying to ask for an update – interruption will slow them down and not win you any bonus points." However, contact the PO about substantive issues (e.g., faculty position contingent on award) and if you have not heard anything after an expected interval.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRO vs PO roles in rebuttal and review follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Review Officer (SRO) handles peer review and produces the summary statement; PO takes over afterward and is the person who may request rebuttals and advocate with IC leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote: "Your PO rather than the SRO would have requested a rebuttal (application will be referred to them by CSR)... SRO involvement stops after summary statement is produced." For rebuttal or advocacy questions, speak to your PO.

rubrics_metrics.name: IC-specific paylines and award rate patterns (R21, R35, K awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different mechanisms and ICs have different typical payline behavior and award patterns; check IC-specific statistics and ask PO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the page: "R21s can have a tougher payline at some ICs, but a 6th percentile application should be funded at any IC." For R35 (NHLBI) there are few awards (4–7/year) so programmatic considerations matter. NIGMS publishes award-rate vs impact score trends (award rates peaking at scores 15–20). Use these IC-specific data to set expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use R56 to generate preliminary data for a stronger R01
rubrics_metrics.description: The R56 is intended as short-term support to produce data that will strengthen a subsequent resubmission or a new competing R01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Page and NIAID SOP guidance: "After you receive an R56-Bridge award, submit an improved R01 using data resulting from the R56 award." Plan R56 activities to produce work that can be cited in the next R01; coordinate scope so R56 work is not duplicated in the subsequent R01 proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding timeline variability and posted timelines are illustrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Award timelines can vary widely across ICs and mechanisms; community-posted timelines can be helpful but individual cases differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple timelines on the page show varied sequences (SRG dates, score release, summary statement, JIT, council, pending administrative review, award). Use timelines as reference and consult PO for case-specific expectations. Example: "your timeline demonstrates that gray zone A0s can be picked up after A1s are submitted and scored."

rubrics_metrics.name: eRA Advisory Council date placeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: eRA Commons may show a single fall date as a placeholder for Council meeting for CSR referral purposes; the Advisory Council section will later show the specific IC/meeting date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanation from page: "eRA Commons uses a single fall date for all council meetings as a placeholder... The meeting date is accurate in the Advisory Council section because it is specific to your IC... You don’t need to worry about the dates not matching."

rubrics_metrics.name: RPPR timing and follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Research Performance Progress Reports (RPPRs) are generally due 60 days before the end of the budget period and delays in processing non-competing continuations can occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quote: "I believe RPPRs are due 60 days before the end of the budget period, so that could explain some delay..." If you see prolonged 'pending administrative review' status, contact your PO to determine next steps and escalate if necessary.
